lines.trans: Look at the left side of the watercolour sketch—there is a tiny carved leaf!
Walk around the dry side of the basin, Nour; do you see it on the stone?
Right here under the spout! A stone leaf pointing northwest up the gentle hill!
Let me read Card Two: Follow the leaf until twelve chimes cast a straight shadow.
Twelve chimes! That has to be the old municipal clock tower three blocks up!
Three blocks up the main street? Nonsense, I know a two-minute shortcut!
Are you sure about this narrow lane, Rami? My compass says that bends south.
I have lived on Jasmine Street for twenty years, Tariq, and alleys beat compasses!
Did you remember to pull your reading glasses down before choosing that turn, Rami?
Who needs reading glasses to recognize a perfectly straight neighbourhood lane?
All right, lead the expedition, Captain, while I count every turn in my notebook.
Left past the flower pots, left again past the green fence—where are we going?!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رسمات.

examples.text: في رسمة مفتاح دهبي فوق الباب.
examples.trans: There is a drawing of a golden key above the door.
His pencil sketches are very detailed.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ألوان.

examples.trans: The colour of the suitcase is dark blue.
The courtyard colours are soothing to the eye.

meanings.note: Relational adjective from ماء ('water'): دهان مائي = 'water-based paint'.

examples.text: الحمد لله الدهان مائي وبيروح بالمي الدافية.
examples.trans: Thankfully the paint is water-based and comes right off with warm water.

examples.text: الدهان المائي ريحته خفيفة وبينشف خلال ساعة.
examples.trans: Water-based paint has a mild smell and dries within an hour.

meanings.note: One sheet of paper or one leaf; the collective ورق means paper in general.

examples.trans: Write your number down for me on a piece of paper.
The tree leaf turns yellow in autumn.

meanings.note: Singulative شجرة ('a tree', feminine), collective شجر ('trees').

examples.trans: We placed the table under the old tree.
We hear the rustle of tree leaves in the courtyard.

meanings.note: The word 'منحوت' (el-manHoote) means 'carved'. It is a common adj in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بسيطة! هادا نافورة الحجر المنحوتة الصغيرة بآخر الشارع تبعنا!
examples.trans: Easy! That is the little carved stone fountain at the end of our block!
This is منحوت.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صغيرة, plural: صغار).

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Common defective verb for walking on foot or things running smoothly.

examples.text: ممنوع تمشي عكاحلك لحد بكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: You mustn't walk on your ankle until tomorrow morning.

examples.text: مشينا عالهدا بالساحة بعد ما وقفت المطر.
examples.trans: We walked gently across the courtyard after the rain stopped.

meanings.note: The word 'حوالي' (Hawaal) means 'around'. It is a common prep in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: امشي حوالي الجهة الناشفة من الحوض يا نور؛ شايفتيها عالحجر؟
examples.trans: Walk around the dry side of the basin, Nour; do you see it on the stone?
This is حوالي.

meanings.note: Used with right and left: الجهة اليمين 'the right side', من هاي الجهة 'from this side'.

examples.trans: The kitchen is on the other side.
Walk this way, it is closer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناشفة, plural: ناشفين).

examples.trans: Here is a dry towel for your coat.
The attic is dry and warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: The word 'حوض' (el-HooD) means 'basin'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: امشي حوالي الجهة الناشفة من الحوض يا نور؛ شايفتيها عالحجر؟
examples.trans: Walk around the dry side of the basin, Nour; do you see it on the stone?
This is حوض.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Active participle of شاف ('to see'), standard in Jordanian for 'I see / do you see?'.

examples.text: شايفة رسمة المفتاح الدهبي فوق الباب!
examples.trans: I see the painted golden key above the door!
Do you see the yellow light in the attic window?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حجار.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth.
She stepped onto the stone step outside.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian/Levantine word for 'here' (لهون 'to here', من هون 'from here').

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Used almost universally in the Levantine adverbial phrase بالزبط (biz-zabt, 'exactly / right on').

examples.text: هاد هو اللون الأخضر اللي بدنا إياه بالزبط!
examples.trans: That is the exact shade of green we want!

examples.text: وصل السايق عالباب الساعة تنتين بالزبط.
examples.trans: The driver arrived at the gate at two o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('under, beneath') and standalone ('downstairs').

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: The word 'مصب' (el-maSabb) means 'spout'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هون بالزبط تحت المصب! ورقة حجر بتأشر للشمال الغربي طالعة التلة الخفيفة!
examples.trans: Right here under the spout! A stone leaf pointing northwest up the gentle hill!
This is مصب.

meanings.note: The word 'أشر' (b-ta'asher) means 'she points'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هون بالزبط تحت المصب! ورقة حجر بتأشر للشمال الغربي طالعة التلة الخفيفة!
examples.trans: Right here under the spout! A stone leaf pointing northwest up the gentle hill!
This is أشر.

meanings.note: The word 'غربي' (el-gharbi) means 'western'. It is a common adj in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هون بالزبط تحت المصب! ورقة حجر بتأشر للشمال الغربي طالعة التلة الخفيفة!
examples.trans: Right here under the spout! A stone leaf pointing northwest up the gentle hill!
This is غربي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طالعة, plural: طالعين).

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading right out!
We are going up to the third floor.

meanings.note: Small hill (plural تلال tilaal); familiar across hilly Amman.

examples.text: عمان مبنية على تلال حلوة بتطل عالسما.
examples.trans: Amman is built across lovely hills looking out at the sky.

examples.text: لما نقسم الشغل الكبير لتلال صغيرة بصير سهل.
examples.trans: When we break a big job into small hills, it becomes easy.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خفيفة, plural: خفاف).

examples.trans: Coffee with milk and light sugar.
A light, tasty breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: Imperative forms with object pronouns give خليكم بحالكم ('stay in your own business') and خلوني بحالي ('leave me in mine').

examples.trans: Let me speak for a bit.
Stay calm, Mariam.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: The word 'اتبع' (itba3oo) means 'follow'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خليني أقرأ الكرت التاني: اتبعوا الورقة لحد ما اطنعشر دقة ترمي خيال مستقيم.
examples.trans: Let me read Card Two: Follow the leaf until twelve chimes cast a straight shadow.
This is اتبع.

meanings.note: Combines with ما before a verb to mean 'until' (لحد ما اتصلت 'until you called').

examples.trans: We waited until you called us.
I stayed up until midnight.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: The word 'اطنعشر' (iTna3shar) means 'twelve'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خليني أقرأ الكرت التاني: اتبعوا الورقة لحد ما اطنعشر دقة ترمي خيال مستقيم.
examples.trans: Let me read Card Two: Follow the leaf until twelve chimes cast a straight shadow.
This is اطنعشر.

meanings.note: Covers daqqa ('a knock / clock chime', pl. دقات) and diqqa ('precision / punctuality', الدقة بالمواعيد).

examples.text: سمعنا اطنعشر دقة من برج الساعة.
examples.trans: We heard twelve chimes from the clock tower.
I always love punctuality.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برمي, بيرمي).

examples.trans: Maybe he tossed my card in the bin.
Do not throw away the old receipt.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian speech, خيال commonly means a cast 'shadow' or 'silhouette' as well as 'imagination'.

examples.text: شفت خيال القطة على الحيط تحت الفانوس.
examples.trans: I saw the cat's shadow on the wall beneath the lantern.

examples.text: خيال الشجرة واصل لحد باب المطبخ.
examples.trans: The tree's shadow reaches right to the kitchen door.

meanings.note: The word 'مستقيم' (mustaqeem) means 'straight'. It is a common adj in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خليني أقرأ الكرت التاني: اتبعوا الورقة لحد ما اطنعشر دقة ترمي خيال مستقيم.
examples.trans: Let me read Card Two: Follow the leaf until twelve chimes cast a straight shadow.
This is مستقيم.

meanings.note: Means 'certainly, definitely' or 'must be' (إنتي أكيد نور 'you must be Nour').

examples.trans: Hello! You must be Nour.

examples.text: أكيد صاحبه رح يدور عليه قريبا.
examples.trans: Surely its owner will look for it soon.

meanings.note: The word 'هادا' (haada) means 'this'. It is a common pron in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بسيطة! هادا نافورة الحجر المنحوتة الصغيرة بآخر الشارع تبعنا!
examples.trans: Easy! That is the little carved stone fountain at the end of our block!
This is هادا.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أبراج.

examples.trans: The downtown clock tower is old.
We heard the tower bell at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساعات.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: From بلد ('country, town'); prized on Jordanian market stalls for local olive oil, honey, lemons, and thyme.

examples.text: عسل بلدي من جبال عجلون ريحته بتشهي.
examples.trans: Local honey from the Ajloun hills smells delicious.
We bought yellow local lemons for tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: The word 'تلات' (tlaat) means 'three'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اطنعشر دقة! أكيد هادا برج الساعة البلدي القديم تلات بلوكات لفوق!
examples.trans: Twelve chimes! That has to be the old municipal clock tower three blocks up!
This is تلات.

meanings.note: The word 'بلوك' (blokkaat) means 'blocks'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اطنعشر دقة! أكيد هادا برج الساعة البلدي القديم تلات بلوكات لفوق!
examples.trans: Twelve chimes! That has to be the old municipal clock tower three blocks up!
This is بلوك.

meanings.note: The word 'لفوق' (lafoq) means 'up'. It is a common adv in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: اطنعشر دقة! أكيد هادا برج الساعة البلدي القديم تلات بلوكات لفوق!
examples.trans: Twelve chimes! That has to be the old municipal clock tower three blocks up!
This is لفوق.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رئيسية, plural: رئيسيين).

examples.trans: We shut off the main water valve in the cellar.
The main gate is on the quiet street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Save the formal talk for later.
That is kind, honest talk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فاضية, plural: فاضيين).

examples.trans: Is room six vacant tonight?
The street outside the gate is completely empty.

meanings.note: Subject pronoun 'I' for any speaker.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعرف, بيعرف).

examples.trans: I recognized your neat handwriting in two seconds!
Do you know anyone here in Amman?

meanings.note: The word 'اختصار' (ikhtiSaar) means 'shortcut'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: تلات بلوكات لفوق بالشارع الرئيسي؟ حكي فاضي، أنا بعرف اختصار بدقيقتين!
examples.trans: Three blocks up the main street? Nonsense, I know a two-minute shortcut!
This is اختصار.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: متأكدة, plural: متأكدين).

examples.trans: Are you sure you do not need this sweater?
I am one hundred percent sure.

meanings.note: The word 'دخلة' (hal-dakhle) means 'this lane'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: متأكد من هالدخلة الضيقة يا رامي؟ بوصلتي بتحكي إنها بتلف للجنوب.
examples.trans: Are you sure about this narrow lane, Rami? My compass says that bends south.
This is دخلة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ضيقة, plural: ضيقين).

examples.trans: The attic stairs are a bit narrow.
Do not enter the narrow alley.

meanings.note: The word 'رامي' (رامي) means 'رامي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: سؤال حلو، لأنه رامي بيمشي كأنه عم يلحق باص رايح!
examples.trans: Good question, because Rami walks like he is chasing a departing bus!
This is رامي.

meanings.note: The word 'بوصلة' (bowSlet) means 'compass'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خلينا نفحص بوصلة النحاس بالأول: الشرق بروح دغري باتجاه مخبز الزاوية.
examples.trans: Let us check the brass compass first: east runs straight toward the corner bakery.
This is بوصلة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Introduces 'that'-clauses with pronoun suffixes (إنه 'that', إني 'that I', إنك 'that you', إنها 'that she/it') and appears in إن شاء الله ('if God wills').

examples.trans: Thank you for coming today.
Do you think that I am a hotel inspector?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلف, بيلف).

examples.text: لفي شمال برا البوابة وامشي دغري.
examples.trans: Turn left outside the gate and walk straight.
Turn left at the stair landing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guests arrived from the south in the morning.
The weather is warm in the south today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ساكنة, plural: ساكنين).

examples.trans: Does your older brother live here in Amman?
We used to live on Jasmine Street years ago.

meanings.note: The word 'الياسمين' (الياسمين) means 'الياسمين'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: شو هالصباح الحلو يوم السبت لمشية كنز بشارع شارع الياسمين!
examples.trans: What a glorious Saturday morning for a treasure walk down Jasmine Street!
This is الياسمين.

meanings.note: Numeral 'twenty' (followed by a singular noun in Arabic: عشرين دقيقة 'twenty minutes').

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سنين.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: The word 'طارق' (طارق) means 'طارق'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أنا ساكن بشارع شارع الياسمين من عشرين سنة يا طارق، والزقاق بيغلب البوصلة!
examples.trans: I have lived on Jasmine Street for twenty years, Tariq, and alleys beat compasses!
This is طارق.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أزقة.

examples.trans: The stone alley is narrow and quiet.
We turned past the narrow lane.

meanings.note: The word 'غلب' (biyghleb) means 'he beats'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أنا ساكن بشارع شارع الياسمين من عشرين سنة يا طارق، والزقاق بيغلب البوصلة!
examples.trans: I have lived on Jasmine Street for twenty years, Tariq, and alleys beat compasses!
This is غلب.

meanings.note: The word 'تذكر' (tdhakkart) means 'you remembered'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: تذكرت تنزل نظارات القراءة تبعتك قبل ما تختار هاللّفة يا رامي؟
examples.trans: Did you remember to pull your reading glasses down before choosing that turn, Rami?
This is تذكر.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: نزل.

examples.text: نزل الساحة فيه تمن غرف هادية.
examples.trans: The courtyard guesthouse has eight quiet rooms.
Welcome to our small guesthouse.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قراءات.

examples.trans: We put a brass reading lamp by the desk.
I love reading in the quiet courtyard.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian possessive word ('belonging to'); agrees in gender: تبع (m.), تبعت (f.), تبعون (pl.).

examples.text: اليوم آخر يوم بأسبوع التجربة تبعك.
examples.trans: Today is the last day of your trial week.
My brother's piano teacher!

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بختار, بيختار).

examples.trans: I chose this quarter for a family reason.
They chose a table under the tree.

meanings.note: Versatile Jordanian noun meaning a wrapped parcel (اللفة البيضا), a pastry roll (لفة قرفة, also pl. لفائف), a street/stair turn (عاللفة), or a wrench turn (لفة، لفتين).

examples.text: أكلت لفة قرفة سخنة مع الشاي.
examples.trans: I ate a warm cinnamon roll with tea.
Watch the tight turn on the stairs.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'who?' (لمين 'whose? / for whom?').

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?
Whose is this brown leather notebook?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحتاج, بيحتاج).

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.
An old house needs steady care.

عشان.gloss: for; because of; in order to

meanings.en: for; because of; in order to
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'for / because of' (عشان هيك 'that is why') and 'so that'.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: The word 'ميز' (ymayyez) means 'he recognizes'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: مين بيحتاج نظارات قراءة عشان يميز دخلة حارة مستقيمة تماما؟
examples.trans: Who needs reading glasses to recognize a perfectly straight neighbourhood lane?
This is ميز.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حارات.

examples.trans: The shop is right here in our neighbourhood.
Old Amman neighbourhoods are peaceful.

meanings.note: Adverb 'exact, completely, perfectly'.

examples.trans: Its size fits you perfectly.
The street is completely empty at noon.

meanings.note: Describes kind-hearted people (ناس طيبين) and pleasant smells/tastes (ريحة طيبة); standalone طيب means 'alright / well then'.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
The coffee smells wonderful in the morning!

meanings.note: The word 'قاد' (qood) means 'lead'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: طيب، قود الحملة يا كابتن، وأنا رح أعد كل لفة بدفتري.
examples.trans: All right, lead the expedition, Captain, while I count every turn in my notebook.
This is قاد.

meanings.note: The word 'حملة' (el-Hamle) means 'expedition'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: طيب، قود الحملة يا كابتن، وأنا رح أعد كل لفة بدفتري.
examples.trans: All right, lead the expedition, Captain, while I count every turn in my notebook.
This is حملة.

meanings.note: The word 'كابتن' (kaabten) means 'captain'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: طيب، قود الحملة يا كابتن، وأنا رح أعد كل لفة بدفتري.
examples.trans: All right, lead the expedition, Captain, while I count every turn in my notebook.
This is كابتن.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Levantine future marker placed before a subjunctive verb (without ب-).

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: The word 'عد' (n3edd) means 'we count'. It is a common verb in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنى يا رامي—خطوات مين عم نعد، خطواتك ولا خطواتي؟
examples.trans: Wait, Rami—whose paces are we counting, yours or mine?
This is عد.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: The word 'يسار' (yasaar) means 'left'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: يسار بعد قواوير الورد، ويسار كمان مرة بعد السور الأخضر—لوين رايحين؟!
examples.trans: Left past the flower pots, left again past the green fence—where are we going?!
This is يسار.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Levantine word (qawwaar, plural qawaawiir) for a clay courtyard plant pot.

examples.text: زرعنا نعنع أخضر بقواوير فخار بالساحة.
examples.trans: We planted green mint in clay pots in the courtyard.

examples.text: سقت نور قوار الليمون جنب الدرج.
examples.trans: Nour watered the lemon pot beside the stairs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ورد.

examples.trans: We walked past the flower stall.
The scent of roses and jasmine filled the courtyard.

كمان.gloss: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)

meanings.en: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)
meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'also, too, more' (كمان مرة 'one more time / again').

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مرات.

examples.trans: The doorbell rang twice.
I read the letter three times.

meanings.note: The word 'سور' (el-soor) means 'fence'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: يسار بعد قواوير الورد، ويسار كمان مرة بعد السور الأخضر—لوين رايحين؟!
examples.trans: Left past the flower pots, left again past the green fence—where are we going?!
This is سور.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: Active participle of راح ('to go'), used like a present progressive in Levantine ('am/is/are going').

examples.text: أنا وسلمى رايحين عالسوق نجيب ليمون.
examples.trans: Salma and I are heading to the market to get lemons.

examples.text: وين رايح بهالسلة الكبيرة يا زياد؟
examples.trans: Where are you heading with that big basket, Ziad?

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: The word 'اللقاء' (اللقاء) means 'اللقاء'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
This is اللقاء.
